**Finding: missing** (medium severity) — no post-termination transition or data-return provision exists.

**What I found:**
- **Section 14 (p0079)** covers only the tail-end of service delivery after a termination notice — nothing about exit.
- **Section 13 (p0078)** actually runs against us: it makes *Client* responsible for arranging a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days. It confirms Client retains ownership of its domains and Client Content, but ownership without a delivery obligation is not a data-return right.
- **Section 10 (Confidentiality)** has no return-or-destroy mechanic, so it is not a fallback source of a data-return obligation.
- Text searches for return/export/migrate/delete/transition turned up nothing relevant (only a Y2K reference and a notices provision).

**Why this is a deviation, not a minor gap:** the clause set fails even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days). Given TrueLink hosts borrower and loan data (expressly named as Client Proprietary Information in p0065), having no contractual right to retrieve it on exit approaches walk-away territory.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a new Section 14a after p0079 at the preferred position — up to six months of transition assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates including Web Site/Client Content migration, return of Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter. The comment offers 90 days of assistance as a fallback if the six-month tail is resisted.
